forecasting.shuffling: none — chronological splits enforced for all series
forecasting.scaler: z-score fitted on the train segment only (verified by leakage_audit in code)

protocol.scaler: z-score fitted on train segment only

row_identity_cross_split_audit.interpretation: row identity = full raw record (leakage if it spans splits); feature collisions = distinct transactions with identical feature vectors (informational, not leakage)

fraud_paysim.excluded_columns: newbalanceOrg/newbalanceDest (dataset authors state frauds are cancelled so post-transaction balances leak the outcome); isFlaggedFraud (upstream detector output — target leakage)
fraud_paysim.threshold_tuning: F1 threshold tuned on validation split only

row_identity_cross_split_audit.interpretation: row identity = full raw record (leakage if it spans splits); feature collisions = distinct transactions with identical feature vectors (informational, not leakage)

fraud_ulb.split_boundary_rule: identical Time values never straddle a split boundary
fraud_ulb.scaler: StandardScaler fitted on train split only

risk.split_rule: stratified random — valid because these datasets are client snapshots without timestamps
risk.scaler: StandardScaler fitted on train split only
risk.model_selection: candidate chosen by VALIDATION PR-AUC (never test)

checks.inference_preprocessing: At inference the business's own observed history is used for z-score scaling — the model never receives any future value, so no future information can leak (the future is unknown at prediction time).

fraud_comparison.protocol: identical chronological test rows for every model; supervised thresholds tuned on validation only

duplicate_cross_split_audit.interpretation: row identity = full raw record (leakage if it spans splits); feature collisions = distinct transactions with identical feature vectors (informational, not leakage)

old_iforest_fraud_v1_as_shipped.note: evaluated with its own leaky preprocessing (scaler fit on the full dataset), on the chronological test rows it never saw as training rows — a fair upper-bound estimate of its real quality

forecasting_comparison.protocol: same chronological 30-day recursive test for every candidate; GRU compared retail-only-trained vs pooled-trained
forecasting_comparison.honest_conclusion: Pooled training improved the Online Retail test (GRU recursive-30d scaled MAE 0.809 -> 0.777) but slightly degraded the Superstore test (0.651 -> 0.725); the net pooled score of the selected GRU (0.751) is within ~0.02 of the retail-only average — i.e. dataset expansion gave broader coverage with essentially neutral-to-positive net effect, NOT an automatic improvement. Deep models beat the naive baseline but the simple MA(7) baseline is competitive (0.858 vs 0.751).

summary: All time-series splits are chronological with no shuffle and train-only scaling; fraud splits are step/time-boundary based and verified so no raw record spans two splits; leakage-prone columns were excluded with documented reasons; the previously-leaky preprocessing pipeline (scaler fitted before the split) was fixed.
